text: A thousand years ago, parchment was too precious to waste.
So when a text was no longer wanted, the scribes scraped it away, and wrote over it.
But ink remembers. Beneath the new words, the old ones stayed.
A page like that is called a palimpsest.
Wikipedia is the largest one ever made.
Every day, a sentence is scraped away, and another is written in its place.
And all we ever read is the top layer.
So we held it up to the light.
Eight hundred and sixty-two thousand versions. Every layer, kept in MariaDB.
Ask what Wikipedia said on any day you choose, and Gemini answers from the words that stood there.
Follow one claim through every rewriting.
See whose hand changed it, to the second.
Nothing we write is ever really gone.
Palimpsest. If Wikipedia ever said it, we can find it, date it, and answer from it.
